Algebra I · Lesson 2.5

Fractions with Variables

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Now the tops and bottoms of fractions hold variables. A fraction bar is division, and a letter on the top or bottom is just an unknown number, so none of the fraction arithmetic from prealgebra changes. The care with signs from 2.4 carries straight over too.

Key idea
A letter is just an unknown number. Every fraction rule from prealgebra still holds when a letter appears. You can multiply top and bottom by the same thing to make an equivalent fraction, find a common denominator, and reduce to lowest terms. None of those rules ever needed the actual value.
Problem
Combine 2c+5cc2​+c5​ into a single fraction over cc. Enter the numerator.
Show a hint
  • The bottoms already match, so you are just counting pieces of size 1cc1​.
Show the full solution
The bottoms already match, so just count the pieces, 2+5=72+5=7​, giving 7cc7​. The bottom stays cc. Gathering more pieces of one size does not change the size of a piece.
Key idea
Same bottom, add the tops. The denominator names the size of each piece, so two copies of 1xx1​ plus five more copies is seven of them, 2x+5x=7xx2​+x5​=x7​. This is the counting of like things from 2.4, with the shared denominator where the shared letter was. The bottom stays the same, because adding more pieces of one size does not change the size of a piece.
Problem
Write 9m+87−4m−3779m+8​−74m−3​ as one fraction over 77. Enter the constant term of the numerator.
Show a hint
  • Subtracting the whole top subtracts both of its terms, the sign-flip from 2.4.
Show the full solution
The minus hits every term of 4m−34m−3, so the top is 9m+8−4m+3=5m+119m+8−4m+3=5m+11 and the constant is 1111​. Drop the flip on the −3−3 and you get 55 instead, which is the usual slip.
Key idea
Reducing means dividing top and bottom by the same nonzero factor. Divide out the common factor and the fraction is in lowest terms, exactly as with numbers. When a variable is present, you often cannot see the common factor until you factor first, the 2.3 move. Pull the shared factor out of the top and the bottom, then divide it away. The factor you cancel has to be nonzero, which every common factor here is.
Problem
Simplify 6n+15336n+15​ by factoring the top and cancelling, then evaluate the result at n=4n=4. Enter the value.
Show a hint
  • Factor the top before cancelling. What divides both 6n6n and 1515?
Show the full solution
Factor the top, 3(2n+5)3=2n+533(2n+5)​=2n+5, and at n=4n=4 that is 8+5=138+5=13​. Cancelling the 33 against only the 1515 is the slip. The 33 has to divide the whole top before it can go.
Problem
A classmate simplifies r+10rrr+10​ to 1010 by crossing out the rr's. Test the original r+10rrr+10​ at r=2r=2, the 1.4 way. Enter its value.
Show a hint
  • Evaluate the untouched fraction and compare with the 1010 the cancel claims.
Show the full solution
At r=2r=2 the untouched fraction is 2+102=122=622+10​=212​=6​, not the 1010 the cancel claims. Here rr is a term of r+10r+10, not a factor of the whole top, so crossing it out is illegal.
Key idea
Only a whole factor cancels. A factor multiplies the entire top and the entire bottom. A term is just one piece of a sum. You may divide away a shared factor, but you may never cross out a single term, because a lone term is not multiplying the whole thing. Crossing out the rr above gave 1010, while the real value was 66, so the illegal cut changed the number. Factor first, then cancel.
Problem
Simplify 8b−40b−5b−58b−40​. Factor the top, cancel the shared (b−5)(b−5), and enter what is left.
Show a hint
  • Nothing cancels until the top is factored. Pull the common factor out of 8b−408b−40.
Show the full solution
Factor the top, 8(b−5)b−5b−58(b−5)​. The whole chunk (b−5)(b−5) is shared, so it divides out and leaves 88​. Nothing cancels until the top is factored, since a loose piece of a sum is not a factor.
Problem
Add 3p+74pp3​+4p7​ over the common denominator 4p4p. Enter the numerator.
Show a hint
  • 4p4p is a multiple of pp. Scale 3pp3​ up by 4444​, an equivalent fraction.
Show the full solution
Scale the first fraction, 3p=124pp3​=4p12​, then add over 4p4p, 12+7=1912+7=19​. Adding 3+73+7 straight across skips the scaling, and the pieces are different sizes until you do it.
Key idea
No shared factor, use the product. When two bottoms share no common factor, their product is always a common denominator. Scale each fraction up to it, the first by the second bottom and the second by the first. Multiply top and bottom by the same thing so each stays an equivalent fraction. Then the bottoms match and you combine the tops.
Problem
Write 3v+24−v−7343v+2​−3v−7​ as one fraction over 1212. Enter the constant term of the numerator.
Show a hint
  • The bottoms 44 and 33 share no factor, so 1212 is their product.
  • Scale each fraction to twelfths, then subtract the whole second top.
Show the full solution
Over 1212 the tops are 3(3v+2)=9v+63(3v+2)=9v+6 and 4(v−7)=4v−284(v−7)=4v−28. The minus takes the whole second top, 9v+6−4v+28=5v+349v+6−4v+28=5v+34, so the constant is 3434​. Miss the flip on the −28−28 and you land at −22−22.
Key idea
Subtracting subtracts the whole top. A subtraction sign in front of a fraction takes away the entire numerator, so once the bottoms match, every sign in that top flips. It is the −1−1 distributed over every term you saw in 2.4, now in fraction form. Miss one sign and the constant comes out wrong. A sum or difference rewritten as a single fraction in lowest terms is the finished form.
Problem
Combine 5f+15f+3−2ff+35f+15​−f2​ into a single fraction of the form 5f+kff5f+k​. Enter kk (typed like -7).
Show a hint
  • Cancel the (f+3)(f+3) chunk in the first fraction first.
  • Then write 55 as 5fff5f​ to subtract the 2ff2​.
Show the full solution
Cancel the shared chunk, 5(f+3)f+3=5f+35(f+3)​=5, then 5−2f=5f−2f5−f2​=f5f−2​, so k=−2k=−2​. Writing 55 as 5fff5f​ is what makes the subtraction possible. 5−2f5−f2​ is not 3ff3​.
Fun fact
Fact. Cancel only a factor shared by the whole top and the whole bottom. A single term of a sum never cancels, no matter how much it looks like the number below it.

Every fraction here had a single letter in it. 2.6 puts several letters in one expression at once. The counting of like pieces and the care with signs work exactly the same way with more letters to track, so the rewrites you just practiced are already the whole toolkit.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Add 4g+5gg4​+g5​. Enter the numerator of the sum over gg.
Show the solution
The bottoms already match, so count the pieces, 4+5=94+5=9​. The bottom stays gg. Adding the bottoms too is the common slip, but gathering more pieces of one size does not change the size of a piece.
Practice
Combine 8k−35−8k−7558k−3​−58k−7​ over 55. Enter the numerator.
Show the solution
The minus hits every term of 8k−78k−7, so 8k−3−8k+7=48k−3−8k+7=4​. Half-flipping to 8k−3−8k−78k−3−8k−7 lands the constant at −10−10, so flip both signs of the second top.
Practice
Simplify 10e+355510e+35​ by factoring the top and cancelling, then evaluate the result at e=3e=3. Enter the value.
Show the solution
Factor the top, 5(2e+7)5=2e+755(2e+7)​=2e+7, and at e=3e=3 that is 6+7=136+7=13​. Cancelling the 55 against only the 3535 is the slip. The 55 has to divide the whole top before it can go.
Practice
A student cancels the hh's in h+15hhh+15​ and writes 1515. Evaluate the original h+15hhh+15​ at h=3h=3, the 1.4 way, and enter the true value.
Show the solution
At h=3h=3 the untouched fraction is 3+153=183=633+15​=318​=6​, not the 1515 the cancel claims. Here hh is a term of h+15h+15, not a factor of the whole top, so crossing it out is illegal.
Practice
Simplify 7c−63c−9c−97c−63​ by factoring the top and cancelling (c−9)(c−9). Enter what is left.
Show the solution
Factor the top, 7(c−9)c−9c−97(c−9)​. The whole chunk (c−9)(c−9) is shared, so it divides out and leaves 77​. Nothing cancels until the top is factored, since a loose piece of a sum is not a factor.
Practice
Simplify 10(x−3)4(x−3)4(x−3)10(x−3)​ by cancelling the shared (x−3)(x−3). Enter the number left, in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The (x−3)(x−3) is a whole factor of both, so it divides out and leaves 104=52410​=25​​. Stopping at 104410​ is the easy miss. The number part still reduces.
Practice
Add 5y+32yy5​+2y3​. Scale the first to halves-of-yy, add over 2y2y, and enter the numerator.
Show the solution
Scale the first fraction, 5y=102yy5​=2y10​, then add over 2y2y, 10+3=1310+3=13​. Adding 5+35+3 straight across skips the scaling, and the pieces are different sizes until you do it.
Practice
The denominators of 4j+7kj4​+k7​ share no factor. Enter their least common denominator, typed like jkjk.
Show the solution
With no shared factor, the product of the bottoms works, so the least common denominator is jkjk​. Neither jj nor kk divides the other, so neither one alone can serve as a common bottom.
Practice
Combine r+32−r−852r+3​−5r−8​ over 1010. The subtraction flips every sign of the second top. Enter the constant term of the combined numerator.
Show the solution
Over 1010 the tops are 5(r+3)=5r+155(r+3)=5r+15 and 2(r−8)=2r−162(r−8)=2r−16. The minus takes the whole second top, 5r+15−2r+16=3r+315r+15−2r+16=3r+31, so the constant is 3131​. Miss the flip on the −16−16 and you land at −1−1.
Practice
In 4x+9xx4x+9​ a student cancels the xx from 4x4x against the bottom and writes 1313. Evaluate the original at x=3x=3 and enter the true value.
Show the solution
Keep the fraction whole and substitute. At x=3x=3 it is 4(3)+93=213=734(3)+9​=321​=7​, not the 1313 the cancel claims. The xx in 4x4x is tied into one term of 4x+94x+9, so it is not a factor of the whole top.
Practice
Combine 4s−36−2s−6364s−3​−32s−6​ into one fraction and reduce. The ss terms cancel. Enter the result in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Scale the second fraction to sixths, 2s−63=4s−12632s−6​=64s−12​. The minus takes the whole top, (4s−3)−(4s−12)=9(4s−3)−(4s−12)=9, so the result is 96=3269​=23​​. Half-flipping to 4s−3−4s−124s−3−4s−12 gives −15−15 instead.
Practice
Simplify 12w4w4w12w​ and enter that number.
Show the solution
Divide top and bottom by the whole shared factor 4w4w, leaving 124=3412​=3​. Cancelling only the ww and stopping at 124412​ is the easy miss, since the numbers still reduce.
